entries.wants: says that a file could not be read because it kept changing while it was being read; {path} is the file
entries.where: error line under a list of files in the terminal interface, one short sentence without a full stop, keeps {path}
entries.text: {path} kept changing while it was being read

entries.wants: says that a shell in the environment {name} cannot be opened because hmz is not running in a terminal
entries.where: red line in the log of the terminal interface, one sentence, keeps {name}
entries.text: A shell in {name} cannot be opened because hmz is not running in a terminal.

entries.wants: how a shell ended: the person left it with ~. and it keeps running in the environment
entries.where: said after `Shell in {name}: ` in the log of the terminal interface, a short phrase with a capital and a full stop

entries.wants: how a shell ended: the connection or the terminal failed, {why} is the reason in the host's words
entries.where: said after `Shell in {name}: ` in the log of the terminal interface, short, keeps {why} at the end after a colon

entries.wants: names the shell that just ended and says how: {name} is the environment, {ended} is a phrase such as `Left; it keeps running.`
entries.where: line in the log of the terminal interface, of the shape `Shell in {name}: {ended}`

entries.wants: says what the list of environments holds: every environment that the chat or epic on screen uses
entries.where: the line under the title Environments of a sheet of the terminal interface, one sentence with a full stop
entries.text: Every environment that this chat or epic uses.

entries.wants: what the tab key does on a sheet of one environment that has several pages (Files, Changes, Terminal, Snapshots): goes to the next page
entries.where: key hint on the bottom line of a sheet of the terminal interface, one or two words, capitalised like the page's button names

entries.wants: says what the list of terminals is for: come back to a terminal left running in this environment, or open a new one
entries.where: the line under the title Terminals of a sheet of the terminal interface, one sentence with a full stop
entries.text: Come back to a terminal left running in this environment, or open a new one.

entries.wants: what the row `New terminal` opens: a new login shell of its own in the environment
entries.where: the muted line beside the row New terminal in a list of the terminal interface, a short phrase in lower case with no full stop
entries.text: a new login shell of its own in this environment

entries.wants: what choosing the confirming answer of a yes-or-cancel question does: it does what was asked
entries.where: the muted line beside a choice in a small box of the terminal interface, a short phrase in lower case with no full stop, saying what picking it does

entries.wants: what choosing Cancel in a yes-or-cancel question does: nothing is changed
entries.where: the muted line beside a choice in a small box of the terminal interface, a short phrase in lower case with no full stop, saying what picking it does

entries.wants: says why the person is asked about a file they edited: since they read it, something else wrote the file on disk
entries.where: the line under the question in a small box of the terminal interface, one sentence with a full stop
entries.text: Something else wrote this file on disk since you read it.

entries.wants: what choosing Reload does when a file changed on disk under an edit: the person's edit is thrown away and the file is read again
entries.where: the muted line beside a choice in a small box of the terminal interface, a short phrase in lower case with no full stop, saying what picking it does
entries.text: throws away your edit and reads the file again

entries.wants: what choosing Keep mine does when a file changed on disk under an edit: the person's edit is written over what is on disk
entries.where: the muted line beside a choice in a small box of the terminal interface, a short phrase in lower case with no full stop, saying what picking it does
entries.text: writes your edit over what is on disk

entries.wants: what choosing Show the diff does when a file changed on disk under an edit: shows what is on disk compared with the person's edit
entries.where: the muted line beside a choice in a small box of the terminal interface, a short phrase in lower case with no full stop, saying what picking it does
entries.text: compares what is on disk with your edit

entries.wants: tells the person that pressing the key e on a file opens it in their own editor ($VISUAL or $EDITOR), said after a sentence saying the file is not opened here
entries.where: error line under a list of files in the terminal interface, one sentence with a full stop, names the key e
entries.text: Press e to open it in your own editor.

entries.wants: says that the file {name} is not text and so is not opened in the editor here
entries.where: error line under a list of files in the terminal interface, one sentence with a full stop, keeps {name}
entries.text: {name} is not text and cannot be opened here.

entries.wants: how many files of the environment are listed to pick one from: {n} files
entries.where: the line under the title Go to file of a sheet of the terminal interface, a count with no full stop, keeps {n}

entries.wants: how many files of the environment are listed to pick one from, {n} files, when the environment has more than were listed
entries.where: the line under the title Go to file of a sheet of the terminal interface, a count with no full stop, keeps {n}

entries.wants: how many lines a search of the environment's files found: {n} lines that contain {query}
entries.where: the line under the title of a sheet of search results in the terminal interface, a count with no full stop, keeps {n} and {query}

entries.wants: how many lines a search of the environment's files found, {n} lines that contain {query}, when there are more matches than were listed
entries.where: the line under the title of a sheet of search results in the terminal interface, a count with no full stop, keeps {n} and {query}
entries.text: {n} lines with {query}, and more not shown
entries.one: {n} line with {query}, and more not shown

entries.wants: title of a diff that compares the file {path} as it is on disk with the person's own edit of it
entries.where: title line of a diff in the terminal interface, keeps {path} first, short, no full stop

entries.wants: says that for the file {path} what is on disk was kept and the person's edit was dropped
entries.where: dim line in the log of the terminal interface, one short sentence without a full stop, keeps {path} first
entries.text: {path}: kept what is on disk and dropped your edit

entries.wants: what the button Stage All Changes does: stages every change
entries.where: the muted line beside a button of a sheet of the terminal interface, a short phrase in lower case starting with a verb, no full stop

entries.wants: what the button Unstage All Changes does: unstages everything that is staged
entries.where: the muted line beside a button of a sheet of the terminal interface, a short phrase in lower case starting with a verb, no full stop

entries.wants: says what rewinding to a snapshot does: the environment's files are put back as they were at that snapshot
entries.where: the line under the title Snapshots of a sheet of the terminal interface, one sentence with a full stop
entries.text: Rewinding puts the environment's files back as they were at that snapshot.

entries.wants: says that `/env {name}` names no environment here, and lists the roles that can be chosen: {roles}
entries.where: error line in the terminal interface, begins with `/env {name}:`, keeps {name} and {roles}

entries.wants: what the key e does on a file in the list of an environment's files: opens it in the person's own editor, the one $EDITOR names
entries.where: key hint on the bottom line of a sheet of the terminal interface, one or two words, capitalised like the page's button names

entries.wants: says that the file {path} edited in the person's own editor was saved back into the environment {name}
entries.where: dim line in the log of the terminal interface, one short sentence without a full stop, starts with a capital, keeps {path} and {name}
